title: SOLAR ARRAY WITH LATCHED SHALLOW CURVED SURFACE FOR IMPROVED DEPLOYED STIFFNESS (ARTES AT 4F.161) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop, manufacture and test a latch to enhance the deployed stiffness of an existing array, by means of a slight repositioning of panels. Targeted Improvements: Increase the frequencies of the deployed array by 30%.Description: Most telecommunication solar arrays comprise in-line panels, arranged in a row. Some include lateral panels, forming a cross configuration. In the case of the latter, the frequency of the first deployed mode is increased, since the offset of the array centre of mass from the spacecraft sidewall is reduced, while maintaining array surface area and consequently power. At system level, deployed appendages need to be of sufficient stiffness to avoid dynamic coupling with the Attitude Orbit Control System. The stiffness of conventional deployed solar arrays is determined by the bending of the panel substrates and hinges. A vastly more effective concept would be one in which the panels act as membranes. This can be achieved by forming a shallow concave (or convex) faceted surface, byintroducing shallow angles between in-line and lateral panels. Extra triangular panels would be needed, to convert cross configurations into oval array shapes. The array would then resemble a spoon, albeit of very shallow depth. For such a concept to work, there would have to be effective load transfer between all panels. While existing hinges could be adapted to provide suitably stiff links between in-line/in-line and in-line/lateral panel junctions, a novel latching mechanism would have to be developed for lateral/lateral panel junctions. Any degradation in power performance, resulting from inter-panel view factors and/or non-optimal incidence angles, would have to be analysed and monitored accordingly. The required triangular panels would not pose a problem, since these can be manufactured in the same manner as flat panels, then cut diagonally. This activity will require a preliminary design, a test plan, the manufacture of a solar array latch breadboard and validation by test. Footnote: On Delegation Request activities will only be initiated on the explicit request of at least one National Delegation.

title: ENGINEERING DATA HUB CONSOLIDATION - EXPRO+
description: Objectives: To complement the Model Based Engineering Data Hub with features related to data governance (security, configuration management), traceability, trade-off, and data exploitation. Description A number of Agencies/industry working groups, such as the Digital Spacecraft Think Tank (DtSC TT) and the Model Based for System Engineering Advisory Group (MB4SE AG), are currently working on the problem of interoperability of tools. Interoperability of tools is supported by a Data Hub in charge of exchanging data. A firstversion is under development. This activity will complement it with the findings by the DtSC TT, mainly on security, configuration management and traceability. It aims at adding features identified in the MB4SE AG's Users Needs such as document generation, automatic budget calculation, trade-off, and dashboard production. It shall complement it with the results of a number of MBSE OSIP and TDE activities currently running and to configure it with the latest version of the Space System Ontology. Complements related to security: (1) mapping of security engineering concepts and semantics to those of system engineering - establishment of security granularity of data sets-, (2) bridging gaps in modelling fidelity between (early phase) system models and that required for security analysis, (3) link to the recent ECSS standards on security, (4) lack of adequate tooling. Complements related to configuration managementof the entire body of system knowledge: Decide on a configuration management policy between the modelling tools, the data hub or the infrastructure backbone. Address data governance and data management resulting from the DtSC data management group. Traceability: To demonstrate the compliance/traceability between the layer of system definition (system level N and N+1) based on model definition. To define a methodology allowing the traceability demonstration between the "needs model based" vs "solution model based" following the system lifecycle management with associated documents. Model based traceability Policy has to be defined to keep trace of the model baseline sources so that a requested update of a document can be performed based on the model relying on the state corresponding to the authoring document generation. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Specification of the missing functionalities;- Design and development;- Verification and validation;- Demonstration on an exchange use case;- Feedback to the ontology as needed.Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence. A future activity could bethe deployment of the Data Hub in an industrial context.

title: INTEGRATED MULTIPLEXER FOR HYBRID SATCOM/TERRESTRIAL 6G USER TERMINALS IN FREQUENCY RANGE 3 (FR3) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7A.081) EXPRO+
description: The objective of the activity is to design, build, and test a wideband multiplexer breadboard supporting 6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks (NTN) in FR3.Targeted Improvements:Enabling building block for hybrid terrestrial/Satcom 6G services.Description: In the frame of 6G developments, the network infrastructure will evolve towards a higher level of integration between the terrestrial network (TN) and the non-terrestrial network (NTN), with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellites playing a significant role in extending coverage and offloading traffic.Frequency Range 3 (FR3) spanning from 7 GHz to 24 GHz, has emerged as a new development area for 6G communications. The spectrum potentially allocated to mobile service on a primary basis includes 7.145 8.5, 10 13.25, 14.3 15.35, 17.7 19.7, and 21.2 23.6 GHz, accumulating in an aggregate bandwidth of approximately 9 GHz. For such systems, a multiband and highly integrated multiplexer would be a key component to enable multiple RF (Radio Frequency) chains to share a common antenna aperture for terminals communicating with both TN/NTN. This feature is particularly attractive in the implementation of hybrid User Terminals for 6G, where up to five bands need to be separated.This activity will develop a wideband multiplexer breadboard using advanced RF filtering and packaging techniques, enabling hybrid terrestrial/satcom 6G NTN services within the same antenna aperture. A review of multiplexing techniques suitable for wideband operation (covering as a minimum the 7 - 24 GHz frequency range) will be carried out with emphasis on filter and multiplexing techniques compatible with monolithic circuit integration,multimode single filter, Air-Filled Substrate Integrated Waveguide, or metamaterials.The activity will trade off and select at least one application scenario (e.g. direct-to-device (D2D), UAVs-supported satellite backhauls) and will produce the detailed design ofa breadboard (5 channels minimum) based on the selected application scenario.Finally, the multiplexer breadboard will be manufactured and tested. The activity shall seek synergies with ongoing flat-panel antenna developments and studies which are outside the scope of this activity. title: Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme eines UAS-gestützten, bathymetrischen LiDAR Sensorsystems sowie Einweisung der Anwender
description: Das ausgeschriebene Scannersystem soll Flachwasserbereiche und Landbereiche durch 3D-Punktwolken erfassen. Zu liefern ist ein System inkl. Mounting und Implementierung für den Betrieb an einer DJI Matrice M400. Die Bestandteile des Systems müssen alle Elemente beinhalten, die nötig sind, um eine RGB-colorierte, klassifizierte 3D-Punktwolke zu generieren. Die Drohne als solche, Windows PC sowie die nötige GNSS-Referenzstation sind NICHT Teil der Ausschreibung. Mithilfe des Systems werden kleinräumige Gebiete oberhalb und unterhalb der Wasseroberfläche drohnenbasiert erfasst. Die Drohnen sowie die für deren Betrieb nötige Expertise sind beim Auftraggeber (AG) vorhanden. Es ist ein bathymetrischer Laserscanner zu liefern, der die Flachwasserbereiche auch unterhalb der Wasseroberfläche bis zu einer bestimmten Sichttiefe (1,5-fach) erfassen kann. Die für die Orientierung und Positionierung nötigen (scannerseitigen) Komponenten sind mitzuliefern bzw. müssen in den Scanner implementiert sein. Dies beinhaltet eine passende IMU, ein GNSS- Modul inkl. zugehöriger Antennen, sowie eine Kamera zur Colorierung der erfassten 3D-Punktwolken. Eine GNSS-Referenzstation bzw. der Zugang zu entsprechenden Korrekturdaten sind AG-seitig vorhanden und damit kein Teil der Ausschreibung. Der Scanner muss so zu betreiben sein, dass seitens des Nutzers bzw. des AG in Bezug auf die erweiterte Augensicherheit (ENOHD (Extendet Norminal Ocular Hazard Distance)) keine weiteren Maßnahmen zu treffen sind. Seitens des Auftragnehmers (AN) sind Vorgaben in Bezug auf Flughöhe und Scanparameter zu geben, die eine entsprechende Augensicherheit am Boden sicherstellen. Es sind alle Elemente zu liefern, die eine dauerhafte und stabile Montage an dem genannten Drohnentyp aber auch eine Demontage mit wenigen Handgriffen ermöglichen. Die Leistung umfasst die Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme des Messsystems, sowie die Einweisung der Anwender. Das zu liefernde System besteht aus folgenden Komponenten: a) bathymetrischer Laserscanner b) Befestigungselemente zur Implementierung in ein System DJI Matrice M400 c) Software zur Trajektorien-Berechnung (1 Lizenz) d) Software zur Ableitung der Punktwolke (1 Lizenz) e) Lieferung des Systems und Einweisung vor Ort Die Lieferung von Hard- und Software muss innerhalb von 8 Wochen nach Erteilung des Zuschlags garantiert werden. Die Einweisung erfolgt nach Terminabstimmung, spätestens jedoch 10 Wochen nach Zuschlagserteilung. Die ausführliche Beschreibung der zu erbringenden Leistungen entnehmen Sie bitte den Vergabeunterlagen.
